a6088.t:
— Says Minister Ngafuan
Finance and Development Planning Minister, Augustine K. Ngafuan, has emphasized that increasing domestic resource mobilization is essential for the country’s growth and development across all sectors. Minister Ngafuan made the remarks during a meeting with a Chinese delegation at the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning on Monday, November 4, 2024.
According to Ngafuan, enhancing domestic resource mobilization will help strengthen governance, fiscal systems, and capital market institutions, reducing the nation's dependency on foreign aid. He added that it would ensure more reliable fiscal revenues, thus reinforcing the social contract between the government and the citizens.
“The leadership of President Boakai is committed to increasing domestic resources across all sectors, aligning them with the National Development Agenda for inclusive growth and development,” Ngafuan stated.
He emphasized that mobilizing local resources is critical not only for enhancing the country’s economic stability but also for enabling citizens to have greater oversight over the use of public funds.
“This will empower citizens to monitor and supervise budgetary revenues and ensure that they are used for the benefit of the people,” Ngafuan explained.
In his remarks, Minister Ngafuan also expressed his gratitude to the Chinese government for their ongoing support to Liberia's health and education sectors.
“Your support over the years has been a source of hope for Liberians across the health and education sectors,” he acknowledged, commending China for its continued assistance.
However, Ngafuan also pointed out two major constraints hindering Liberia’s growth—energy and road infrastructure. He noted that these are the critical areas the government is currently addressing with the help of its development partners.
“Energy and roads are the two huge binding constraints that need a robust solution for our country,” Ngafuan said, underscoring the importance of addressing these issues for sustainable development.
The Liberian government is working towards qualifying for Compact Two, a partnership that would provide further support to key infrastructure projects. According to Ngafuan, the country has already met 14 out of 20 criteria required to qualify for the program.
“Our job is to continue showing progress to our people because they deserve better lives, and we are making significant strides toward that,” he added.
Ngafuan further outlined that one of the major projects underway is the construction of a hydro-energy facility on the St. Paul River, estimated to cost around US$800 million. This project is part of the government’s effort to increase power generation capacity, with solar power also being explored as an alternative source.
“We are going to make reforms to the electricity sector across the country and strengthen accountable institutions like the General Auditing Commission, which has been rolling out many audit processes,” Ngafuan stated.
The Chinese delegation, which praised Ngafuan's leadership, expressed their commitment to supporting Liberia’s development efforts. Ambassador YIN Chengwu, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China, reiterated China’s strong partnership with Liberia and affirmed their continued support for the country’s national development.
“We are willing to support any of your national development and infrastructure projects across Liberia,” Ambassador YIN said, highlighting China’s willingness to assist in various sectors of Liberia’s growth.
Ambassador YIN also took the opportunity to reflect on the strong bilateral ties between Liberia and China. He noted the two countries’ shared experiences in combating Ebola and COVID-19 and their fruitful cooperation in various areas of national development.
“Liberia and China enjoy a long-standing, friendly relationship. In recent years, the Chinese and Liberian people have stood together in the joint fight against Ebola and COVID-19 and have engaged in sincere cooperation in the cause of national development,” he stated.
Since the resumption of bilateral relations in 2003, China has played an increasingly important role in Liberia's reconstruction and peace-building efforts. In 2012, China granted Liberia a duty-free trade agreement on 95% of its exports to China, further strengthening the economic ties between the two nations.
The continued cooperation between Liberia and China is seen as a critical aspect of the country’s development, as both nations work together to address the pressing challenges of infrastructure, energy, and governance. Minister Ngafuan’s statements highlight the government’s focus on strengthening domestic resource mobilization, while also reaffirming the importance of international partnerships in securing Liberia’s long-term growth and development.

a6192.t:
Muktasari:
- Taarifa za Shirika la Wakimbizi la Umoja wa Mataifa (UNHCR) zinaeleza zaidi ya watu 400,000 wamekimbia makazi yao tangu mwanzoni mwa mwaka 2025 kutokana na mapigano hayo.
Dar es Salaam. Mapigano yanayondelea Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasi ya Congo (DRC) yameendelea kusababisha mauaji na ukiukwaji wa haki za binadamu, ikiwamo ubakaji wa raia na vurugu kwenye balozi sita nchini humo.
Mapigano hayo yanayohusisha majeshi ya Serikali ya DRC dhidi ya kikundi cha waasi cha M23 ambacho kimetengaza kuuteka mji wa Goma ikiwamo kuushika uwanja wa ndege wa kimataifa uliopo kwenye mji huo.
Kuendelea kwa mapigano hayo kumewafanya viongozi katika Umoja wa Mataifa, Umoja wa Afrika na Jumuiya ya Maendeleo Kusini mwa Afrika (SADC) kuitisha vikao vya dharura.
Vikao hivyo vilivyoitishwa juzi Januari 28, 2025 ni Baraza la Amani na Usalama (PSC) la Umoja wa Afrika lililokutana kwa ngazi ya mawaziri, Baraza la Usalama la Umoja wa Mataifa na Kamati ya Usalama ya Jumuiya ya Maendeleo Kusini mwa Afrika (SADC-Troika), chini ya mwenyekiti wake Rais Samia Suluhu Hassan.
Kwa mujibu wa taarifa mashirika ya haki za binadamu yamekishutumu kikundi cha M23 kwa ukiukaji wa haki za binadamu, ikiwa ni pamoja na mauaji na ubakaji wa raia.
Taarifa za Shirika la Umoja wa Mataifa la Wakimbizi (UNHCR) zinaeleza zaidi ya watu 400,000 wamekimbia makazi yao tangu mwanzoni mwa mwaka huu kutokana na mapigano hayo.
Pia, mashirika ya misaada yalisema kuwa hospitali zimefurika mamia ya watu waliojeruhiwa katika mapigano wakiwemo watoto.
Shirika la Mpango wa Chakula Duniani (WFP) limesema kuwa usambazaji wa misaada ya chakula umesitishwa kwa muda ndani na karibu na mji huo kutokana na mapigano hayo.
Pia, Msemaji wa ofisi ya Umoja wa Mataifa ya masuala ya kibinadamu, Jens Laerke amesema kulikuwa na miili mingi ya watu waliouawa mitaani.
Kwa mujibu wa taarifa hizo, kati ya waliouawa ni bondia maarufu wa DRC, Balezi Bagunda.
Pia, Shirika la Msalaba Mwekundu limetoa tahadhari kuwa kuendelea kwa mapigano kwenye mji wa Goma kunahatarisha kuenea kwa magonjwa hatari, ikiwemo Ebola, ikiwa maabara zinazohifadhi sampuli za virusi hivyo zitaharibiwa na vurugu.
Katika mji mkuu wa Kinshasa, waandamanaji wamekusanyika na kuchoma moto mbele ya balozi mbalimbali za mataifa ya Magharibi na Afrika, ikiwemo Rwanda.
Ofisi zingine za ubalozi zilizovamiwa na waandamaji hao ni za nchi za Uganda, Kenya, Ufaransa, Marekani na Ubelgiji.
Waandamanaji hao walikuwa wanadai hatua zichukuliwe dhidi ya mashambulizi ya waasi wa M23 katika mashariki mwa DRC.
Pia, mapigano hayo yamesabisha vifo vya watu zaidi ya 25 huku 367 wakijeruhiwa kutokana na majibizano ya risasi mjini Goma.
Mbali na mauaji ya raia pia wanajeshi wa kulinda amani kutoka Afrika Kusini wameripotiwa kuuawa kwenye mapigano hayo na Serikali ya nchi hiyo imethibitisha.
Mji wa Goma ni kitovu cha biashara katika miji iliyopo mashariki mwa DRC.
DRC yaandika barua AU
Kuendelea kwa mapigano yao kumeilazimu Serikali ya Rais Felix Tshisekedi wa DRC kuandika barua kwenye Baraza la Amani na Usalama (PSC) la Umoja wa Afrika (AU) akiomba kuitishwa kwa mkutano wa dharura.
Mkutano huo uliofanyika Januari 28, 2025 kwa ngazi ya mawaziri ambao walikutana kujadili kuendelea kwa mapigano kwenye eneo la Goma.
Iliezwa PSC itasikiliza maoni kutoka kwa wawakilishi wa Angola ambao ni Mwenyekiti wa Mkutano wa Kimataifa wa Ukanda wa Maziwa Makuu (ICGLR), Tanzania ambao ni Mwenyekiti wa Kamati ya Usalama ya Jumuiya ya Maendeleo Kusini mwa Afrika (SADC-Troika) na Kenya ambao ni Mwenyekiti wa Jumuiya ya Afrika Mashariki (EAC).
Pia, PSC ilitarajiwa kupokea taarifa kutoka kwa Mwakilishi Maalumu wa Katibu Mkuu wa Umoja wa Mataifa katika DRC na Mkuu wa Ujumbe wa Umoja wa Mataifa wa Kudumisha Amani DRC (Momusco).
Rais Felix Tshisekedi ndiye Mwenyekiti wa SADC, wakati Rwanda ambayo haiko SADC ni wanachama wa EAC na mwenyekiti wake ni Rais William Ruto wa Kenya.
Tamko la mkutano wa PSC linatarajiwa kulaani ukiukwaji wa mkataba wa kusitisha mapigano, likitaka kusitishwa kwa mapigano na kuondolewa kwa M23 kutoka maeneo iliyoyateka.
PSC pia inaweza kupendekeza kuanzishwa kwa chombo cha usimamizi wa mkataba wa kusitisha mapigano na kuhimiza mazungumzo zaidi chini ya Mchakato wa Luanda.
Baraza hilo linatarajiwa pia kutoa wito wa kuheshimiwa kwa mamlaka na mipaka ya DRC, kuzitaka Rwanda na DRC kujizuia dhidi ya hatua zinazoweza kuchochea mgogoro zaidi na kupendekeza kutumwa kwa ujumbe wa ngazi ya juu kwa Kinshasa na Kigali ili kusaidia upatanishi wa haraka.
Rwanda inadaiwa kuunga mkono kikundi cha waasi cha M23, madai ambayo Rwanda imekuwa ikiyakanusha.
Hayo yakiendelea, taarifa zilizopatikana leo Jumatano Januari 29, ni kuwa wakati nchi za Marekani, Uingereza na Ufaransa, zimekemea kitendo cha Rwanda kuliunga mkono kundi la waasi la M23, Serikali ya Marekani imelitaka Baraza la Usalama la Umoja wa Mataifa kutafakari hatua za kusitisha mapigano hayo.
Waziri wa Mambo ya Nje wa Marekani, Marco Rubio, ameliomba Baraza la Usalama la Umoja wa Mataifa kutafakari hatua za kusitisha mashambulizi yanayofanywa na wanajeshi wa Rwanda na waasi wa M23 mashariki mwa DRC, huku mgogoro huo ukizidi kupamba moto.
Amesema kuwa Marekani inataka kusitishwa kwa mapigano hayo na kuzitaka pande zote kuheshimu mipaka ya ardhi ya taifa huru.
Pia, ubalozi wa Marekani mjini Kinshasa, DRC umewataka raia wake kuondoka katika mji wa Goma kwa sababu ya ongezeko la ghasia.
Barua Umoja wa Mataifa
Pia, Serikali ya DRC ilituma barua kwa Baraza la Usalama la Umoja wa Mataifa Desemba 17, 2024 ikilaumu Rwanda kwa kuchelewesha mazungumzo kwa kushinikiza mazungumzo ya moja kwa moja na M23.
Rwanda ilikanusha shutuma hizo kupitia majibu yake ya Desemba 19, 2024.
Baraza la Usalama lilipokutana kwa dharura kwa mara ya pili ndani ya siku tatu kujadili hali inayozidi kuzorota DRC, ilielezwa mashambulizi yanayoongezeka ya kundi la M23 yanaendelea kuua raia na askari wa kulinda amani ndani na karibu na jiji la Goma.
Kikao cha dharura cha Troika
Kufuatia kuendelea mapigano, Mwenyekiti wa Troika, Rais Samia Suluhu Hassan naye juzi aliitisha mkutano wa dharura.
Mkutano huo ulifanyika Januari 28, 2025, Ikulu Jijini Dar es Salaam, huku mapigano hayo yakitajwa kuwa sababu ya mkutano huo.
Mkutano huo ulioongozwa na Rais Samia, ulihudhuriwa na Rais wa Zambia, Hakainde Hichilema na Rais wa Malawi, Dk Lazarus Chakwera.
Pia, ulihudhuriwa kwa njia ya mtandao na marais Cyril Ramaphosa wa Afrika Kusini na Felix Tshisekedi wa DRC.
Pia, viongozi wa Afrika Mashariki wanapanga kukutana chini ya mwenyekiti wake Rais wa Kenya, William Ruto.
Jitihada za usuluhishi
Tangu 2012, kundi la M23 limekuwa tishio katika maeneo ya Kivu na Ituri, ambapo ilizidi kuimarisha harakati zake za kijeshi tangu Machi 2022.
Katika Mkutano wa Dharura wa AU Mei 2022, Rais wa Angola, João Lourenço, aliteuliwa kuwa msuluhishi wa mgogoro baina ya Rwanda na DRC.
Ingawa alifanikiwa kusaidia kufanikisha mkataba wa kusitisha mapigano Julai 2024, mazungumzo yaliingia kwenye mkwamo Desemba 2024.
Kikao cha ana kwa ana kati ya Rais Tshisekedi na Rais wa Rwanda, Paul Kagame, kilipaswa kufanyika Desemba 15, 2024, lakini kiliahirishwa dakika za mwisho kwa ombi la mmoja wa wahusika.
Mgogoro ulivyozuka
DRC imekuwa ikikumbwa na machafuko ya wanamgambo kwa miongo kadhaa, likiwamo kundi la waasi la M23 linalodai kutetea masilahi ya jamii za wachache wanaozungumza Kinyarwanda, wakiwemo Watutsi.
Tangu mwaka 2022, Kundi la M23 lilianzisha uasi mpya dhidi ya Serikali ya DRC, ikiteka maeneo makubwa ya Kivu Kaskazini, mkoa unaopakana na Rwanda na Uganda.
Kwa miezi kadhaa, waasi wamekuwa wakidhibiti Rubaya, mji wa madini wenye mojawapo ya akiba kubwa zaidi ya madini ya coltan duniani, madini yanayotumika katika utengenezaji wa simu za mkononi.
Ripoti ya Desemba kutoka kwa Kundi la Wataalamu wa Umoja wa Mataifa ilisema kuwa angalau tani 150 za coltan zilisafirishwa kimagendo hadi Rwanda na kuchanganywa na madini ya Rwanda.
Ripoti hiyo iliongeza kuwa: "Tangu Aprili mwaka 2024, M23 kwa msaada wa RDF (Jeshi la Ulinzi la Rwanda), imepata mafanikio ya kidhibiti maeneo mapya."
Hata hivyo, Rwanda imekanusha madai hayo, ikisema kuwa mgogoro huo unahusisha masuala ya ndani ya DRC.
Kwa nini Goma ni lulu
Goma ni mji mkubwa zaidi wa Kivu Kaskazini na ni makazi ya takriban watu milioni mbili.
Ni mji wa kimkakati, wenye uwanja wa ndege wa kimataifa na upakana na Ziwa Kivu, unaofungua njia rahisi kuelekea Kivu Kusini na Rwanda.
Pia, Goma ni kitovu cha shughuli za misaada ya kibinadamu kote mashariki mwa DRC.
a6192.en:
Summary:
- Reports from the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) state that more than 400,000 people have fled their homes since the beginning of 2025 because of the fighting.

Dar es Salaam. The ongoing fighting in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has continued to cause killings and human rights violations, including the rape of civilians and violence at six embassies in the country.

The fighting involves the DRC government forces against the M23 rebel group, which has declared that it has captured the city of Goma, including seizing the international airport located in that city.

The continuation of the fighting has led leaders at the United Nations, the African Union and the Southern African Development Community (SADC) to convene emergency meetings.

Those meetings, convened the day before yesterday, 28 January 2025, were the African Union Peace and Security Council (PSC), which met at ministerial level, the United Nations Security Council, and the Southern African Development Community's security committee (SADC-Troika), under its chair President Samia Suluhu Hassan.

According to reports, human rights organisations have accused the M23 group of human rights violations, including the killing and rape of civilians.

Reports from the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) state that more than 400,000 people have fled their homes since the beginning of this year because of the fighting.

Also, aid organisations said that hospitals have been overwhelmed with hundreds of people wounded in the fighting, including children.

The World Food Programme (WFP) has said that the distribution of food aid has been temporarily suspended in and around that city because of the fighting.

Also, the spokesperson of the United Nations office for humanitarian affairs, Jens Laerke, has said there were many bodies of people who had been killed lying in the streets.

According to those reports, among those killed is the well-known DRC boxer Balezi Bagunda.

Also, the Red Cross has warned that the continuation of the fighting in the city of Goma risks the spread of dangerous diseases, including Ebola, if the laboratories holding samples of that virus are destroyed in the violence.

In the capital Kinshasa, protesters gathered and set fires in front of various Western and African embassies, including Rwanda's.

Other embassy offices stormed by those protesters were those of Uganda, Kenya, France, the United States and Belgium.

Those protesters were demanding that action be taken against the attacks by the M23 rebels in eastern DRC.

Also, the fighting has caused the deaths of more than 25 people while 367 were wounded as a result of the exchanges of gunfire in Goma.

Besides the killing of civilians, peacekeeping soldiers from South Africa have also been reported killed in the fighting and that country's government has confirmed it.

The city of Goma is the commercial hub among the cities of eastern DRC.

DRC writes a letter to the AU

The continuation of the fighting has compelled the government of President Felix Tshisekedi of the DRC to write a letter to the African Union (AU) Peace and Security Council (PSC) requesting that an emergency meeting be convened.

That meeting was held on 28 January 2025 at ministerial level, with ministers meeting to discuss the continuing fighting in the Goma area.

It was stated that the PSC would hear views from the representatives of Angola, which chairs the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR), Tanzania, which chairs the Southern African Development Community's security committee (SADC-Troika), and Kenya, which chairs the East African Community (EAC).

Also, the PSC was expected to receive a briefing from the Special Representative of the United Nations Secretary-General in the DRC and Head of the United Nations Peacekeeping Mission in the DRC (Monusco).

President Felix Tshisekedi is the Chair of SADC, while Rwanda, which is not in SADC, is a member of the EAC, whose chair is President William Ruto of Kenya.

The communique of the PSC meeting is expected to condemn the violation of the ceasefire agreement, demanding a halt to the fighting and the withdrawal of M23 from the areas it has seized.

The PSC may also propose the establishment of a body to oversee the ceasefire agreement and encourage further talks under the Luanda Process.

The Council is also expected to call for respect for the sovereignty and borders of the DRC, to call on Rwanda and the DRC to refrain from steps that could further inflame the conflict, and to propose the dispatch of a high-level mission to Kinshasa and Kigali to assist with rapid mediation.

Rwanda is alleged to support the M23 rebel group, allegations which Rwanda has consistently denied.

As this goes on, reports received today, Wednesday 29 January, are that while the United States, Britain and France have condemned Rwanda's act of supporting the M23 rebel group, the United States government has asked the United Nations Security Council to consider measures to halt the fighting.

The Secretary of State of the United States, Marco Rubio, has asked the United Nations Security Council to consider steps to halt the attacks being carried out by Rwandan troops and M23 rebels in eastern DRC, as the conflict continues to intensify.

He said that the United States wants the fighting to stop and called on all sides to respect the borders of a sovereign nation.

Also, the United States embassy in Kinshasa, DRC, has urged its citizens to leave the city of Goma because of the increase in violence.

Letter to the United Nations

Also, the DRC government sent a letter to the United Nations Security Council on 17 December 2024 blaming Rwanda for delaying talks by insisting on direct negotiations with M23.

Rwanda denied those accusations in its response of 19 December 2024.

When the Security Council met in emergency session for the second time within three days to discuss the deteriorating situation in the DRC, it was stated that the increasing attacks by the M23 group continue to kill civilians and peacekeeping soldiers in and around the city of Goma.

Emergency meeting of the Troika

Following the continuation of the fighting, the Chair of the Troika, President Samia Suluhu Hassan, also convened an emergency meeting the day before yesterday.

That meeting was held on 28 January 2025 at State House in Dar es Salaam, with the fighting cited as the reason for the meeting.

That meeting, chaired by President Samia, was attended by the President of Zambia, Hakainde Hichilema, and the President of Malawi, Dr Lazarus Chakwera.

It was also attended online by Presidents Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa and Felix Tshisekedi of the DRC.

Also, East African leaders plan to meet under their chair, President William Ruto of Kenya.

Mediation efforts

Since 2012, the M23 group has been a threat in the Kivu and Ituri areas, where it has further intensified its military activities since March 2022.

At the AU Emergency Summit in May 2022, the President of Angola, Joao Lourenco, was appointed as mediator of the conflict between Rwanda and the DRC.

Although he succeeded in helping to secure a ceasefire agreement in July 2024, the talks reached a deadlock in December 2024.

A face-to-face meeting between President Tshisekedi and the President of Rwanda, Paul Kagame, was due to take place on 15 December 2024, but it was postponed at the last minute at the request of one of the parties.

How the conflict erupted

The DRC has been afflicted by militia unrest for several decades, including the M23 rebel group which claims to defend the interests of Kinyarwanda-speaking minority communities, including the Tutsi.

Since 2022, the M23 group launched a new rebellion against the DRC government, seizing large areas of North Kivu, a province bordering Rwanda and Uganda.

For several months, the rebels have controlled Rubaya, a mining town with one of the world's largest reserves of coltan, a mineral used in the manufacture of mobile phones.

A December report from the United Nations Group of Experts said that at least 150 tonnes of coltan were smuggled to Rwanda and mixed with Rwandan minerals.

That report added: "Since April 2024, M23 with the support of the RDF (Rwanda Defence Force) has made gains in controlling new areas."

However, Rwanda has denied those allegations, saying that the conflict involves internal DRC matters.

Why Goma is a jewel

Goma is the largest city of North Kivu and is home to approximately two million people.

It is a strategic city, with an international airport, and it borders Lake Kivu, opening an easy route towards South Kivu and Rwanda.

Also, Goma is the hub of humanitarian aid operations across eastern DRC.

a6285.t:
The Delta State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has praised the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) for arresting former Delta State Governor Ifeanyi Okowa, describing the move as a “bold step” in Nigeria’s ongoing anti-corruption campaign.
However, the People’s Democratic Party (PDP), the ruling party in Delta State, condemned the arrest, calling it a “political witch hunt” by the APC-led federal government aimed at silencing opposition voices.
In a statement by APC State Publicity Secretary Valentine Onojeghuo, the party urged the EFCC to widen its investigation to include other officials suspected of financial mismanagement. “Dr. Ifeanyi Okowa’s administration has long been plagued by allegations of financial misconduct and diversion of public funds, which must now be fully addressed,” Onojeghuo said.
Onojeghuo added that the arrest should act as a deterrent to other public officials, asserting, “The era of impunity is over. No one is above the law, regardless of their position or connections.” He further stressed the importance of ensuring that public resources serve the people rather than personal interests, saying, “This is a vital step towards restoring public trust.”
- Trump and Musk can bring peace to golf – McIlroy
- Invictus Games: FG, African Unconquered Foundationseal deal on wounded soldiers’ empowerment
In a prompt response, Timothy Osadolor, the PDP Deputy National Youth Leader, argued that Delta State has not reported any missing funds and insisted that detaining Okowa without formal charges undermines democratic principles.
Okowa, who served as governor from 2015 to 2023, was detained on allegations of embezzling state funds, including the suspected diversion of 13 percent derivation funds designated for Delta State’s development. According to the EFCC, the alleged misappropriation involves approximately N1.3 trillion.

a6573.t:
By MUBITA KATETE
IN a sweeping nationwide crackdown, the Drug Enforcement Commission (DEC) has arrested one of the country’s most elusive drug lords, Henry Shula Kasolo, marking a significant victory in the war against transnational drug trafficking.
 Mr Kasolo, 53, a prominent Lusaka resident of the upscale Leopards Hill area, was captured on Thursday following months of intense surveillance.
 Authorities seized 117 packs of high-grade compressed cannabis weighing 73.9 kilogrammes, which were hidden in four suitcases.
 The operation also netted US$10, 200 and K6, 000 in suspected proceeds of crime, as well as a Toyota Hilux allegedly used in the trafficking scheme.
 “This arrest is a major milestone in our ongoing efforts to dismantle criminal drug syndicates operating both locally and internationally,” DEC Public Relations Officer Allan Tamba said in a press statement.
 “Mr Kasolo has been on our radar for some time, and his apprehension sends a strong message that no one is beyond the reach of justice.”
 In a dramatic twist during his arrest, Mr Kasolo attempted to bribe officers with K60, 000 in a failed bid to secure his release and that of his alleged accomplices – two Thai nationals identified as Phuwanat Hansongkram, 25, and Den Wangngae, 30.
 The pair were found with Baht 24, 620, believed to be illicit proceeds.
 DEC also confirmed that Mr Kasolo is linked to a 2024 case involving the attempted smuggling of 204.7 kilogrammes of cannabis disguised as catalytic powder through Kenneth Kaunda International Airport, destined for Europe.
 “Mr Kasolo was also recently deported from the United States where he was convicted on similar charges,” Mr Tamba added. “This highlights the global footprint of his criminal activities.”
 Also arrested in connection with the same case was 60-year-old Humphrey Alick Chama, a Lusaka resident of New Kasama.
 In a separate DEC-led operation in Lusaka’s Makeni area, 46-year-old Kenyan Maulid Hamud Idris was arrested for trafficking in 21.2 kilogrammes of Mirra (Khat), a stimulant commonly smuggled from East Africa.
 In Livingstone, DEC officers arrested two men from Kazungula, Kasendema Musonda, 33, and Luke Ndimba, 29 for possession of 15.2 and 3.8 kilogrammes of compressed cannabis, respectively.
 All suspects remain in custody pending court appearances.
 Ends.

a6642.t:
Numa publicação na rede social X, o PMA confirmou que "a recente pausa relativa à assistência alimentar em espécie ao PMA (adquirida a agricultores norte-americanos com fundos do Título II) foi revogada".
O chamado Título II da Lei de Alimentos para a Paz (Título II) é um modelo de financiamento tradicionalmente utilizado para fornecer bens alimentares adquiridos nos Estados Unidos a beneficiários em situação de insegurança alimentar no estrangeiro.
O fim da suspensão implica "a retoma das compras e entregas de alimentos ao abrigo dos acordos existentes da USAID (Agência dos Estados Unidos para o Desenvolvimento Internacional)" e permitirá à agência da ONU continuar a trabalhar com as ONG parceiras, "que desempenham um papel vital na distribuição de assistência alimentar de emergência às pessoas afetadas por guerras, inundações, secas e outros desastres em todo o mundo".
"O PMA continua a trabalhar em estreita colaboração com os seus homólogos norte-americanos e com todos os nossos dadores para garantir uma assistência alimentar de emergência constante e ininterrupta nos pontos críticos de fome, incluindo o Sudão, o Sudão do Sul, Gaza, o Haiti e outras áreas em crise", concluiu a agência da ONU.
a6642.en:
The UN announces the resumption of purchases of US food aid through USAID

In a post on the social network X, the WFP confirmed that "the recent pause relating to in-kind food assistance to the WFP (purchased from North American farmers with Title II funds) has been revoked".

The so-called Title II of the Food for Peace Act (Title II) is a funding model traditionally used to supply food commodities purchased in the United States to food-insecure beneficiaries abroad.

The end of the suspension entails "the resumption of food purchases and deliveries under existing USAID (United States Agency for International Development) agreements" and will allow the UN agency to continue working with partner NGOs, "which play a vital role in distributing emergency food assistance to people affected by wars, floods, droughts and other disasters around the world".

"The WFP continues to work closely with its North American counterparts and with all our donors to ensure constant and uninterrupted emergency food assistance in hunger hotspots, including Sudan, South Sudan, Gaza, Haiti and other crisis areas," the UN agency concluded.

a6646.t:
Le Sénégal a réaffirmé, à New York, sa reconnaissance de la souveraineté totale du Maroc sur son Sahara, ainsi que son soutien constant à l’initiative d’autonomie présentée par le Royaume pour clore définitivement ce différend régional.
« Le Sénégal voudrait réaffirmer sans ambiguïté sa reconnaissance de la souveraineté totale du Royaume du Maroc sur le Sahara », a souligné, lundi, le représentant du Sénégal devant les membres de la 4è Commission de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies.
Il a relevé que cette position est matérialisée sur le terrain par une forte présence de ressortissants sénégalais dans les provinces du Sud du Royaume et par l’installation depuis avril 2021 d’un consulat général à Dakhla.
Le diplomate sénégalais a, en outre, réitéré le soutien « constant » de son pays à l’Initiative marocaine d’autonomie que le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU qualifie de sérieuse et crédible dans ses résolutions successives depuis 2007.
Soutenue par plus de 100 Etats membres de l’ONU, cette initiative est consolidée par les réalisations substantielles du Maroc en matière des droits de l’Homme, notamment le rôle joué par les Commissions du Conseil national des droits de l’Homme à Dakhla et Laâyoune, saluées par le Conseil de sécurité dans sa résolution 2703, a noté l’e représentant du Sénégal.
Et d’ajouter que le plan d’autonomie est également consolidé par les investissements et les projets mis en œuvre par le Royaume dans le cadre du nouveau modèle de développement pour les provinces du Sud, contribuant ainsi à l’autonomisation des populations et à l’amélioration de l’indice de développement humain dans la région.
Le diplomate sénégalais a, de même, réaffirmé le « soutien total » à toute « initiative allant dans le sens du bien-être des populations du Sahara marocain et de l’intégrité et la continuité du territoire du Royaume du Maroc ».
Il a par ailleurs salué le plein respect du cessez-le-feu par le Maroc ainsi que sa coopération constante avec la MINURSO, appelant les parties à une meilleure collaboration avec les entités onusiennes notamment le HCR et le PAM pour une prise en charge optimale des droits des populations des camps de Tindouf, en l’occurrence leur liberté d’expression et d’association et l’accès à l’aide humanitaire internationale qui leur est destinée.
Le diplomate a, par la même occasion, salué les efforts de l’Envoyé personnel du Secrétaire général de l’ONU pour le Sahara marocain, Staffan de Mistura, visant à faciliter la relance du processus politique sous les auspices exclusifs des Nations Unies.
Il a appelé les acteurs principaux de ce différend régional à plus d’engagement pour parvenir à une solution politique réaliste et durable, conformément au droit international et aux résolutions pertinentes adoptées par le Conseil de sécurité et l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU.
RT/ac/Sf/APA
a6646.en:
Dakar reaffirms support for Morocco's sovereignty over the Sahara

Senegal reaffirmed, in New York, its recognition of Morocco's full sovereignty over its Sahara, as well as its constant support for the autonomy initiative presented by the Kingdom to definitively close this regional dispute.

"Senegal would like to reaffirm unambiguously its recognition of the full sovereignty of the Kingdom of Morocco over the Sahara," Senegal's representative stressed on Monday before the members of the Fourth Committee of the United Nations General Assembly.

He noted that this position is materialised on the ground by a strong presence of Senegalese nationals in the Kingdom's southern provinces and by the establishment, since April 2021, of a consulate general in Dakhla.

The Senegalese diplomat further reiterated his country's "constant" support for the Moroccan autonomy initiative, which the UN Security Council has qualified as serious and credible in its successive resolutions since 2007.

Supported by more than 100 UN member states, this initiative is consolidated by Morocco's substantial achievements in the field of human rights, notably the role played by the commissions of the National Human Rights Council in Dakhla and Laayoune, hailed by the Security Council in its resolution 2703, the representative of Senegal noted.

He added that the autonomy plan is also consolidated by the investments and projects implemented by the Kingdom under the new development model for the southern provinces, thereby contributing to the empowerment of the populations and the improvement of the human development index in the region.

The Senegalese diplomat likewise reaffirmed "total support" for any "initiative going in the direction of the well-being of the populations of the Moroccan Sahara and of the integrity and continuity of the territory of the Kingdom of Morocco."

He also welcomed Morocco's full respect for the ceasefire as well as its constant cooperation with MINURSO, calling on the parties for better collaboration with UN entities, notably UNHCR and the WFP, for optimal protection of the rights of the populations of the Tindouf camps, in particular their freedom of expression and association and their access to the international humanitarian aid intended for them.

On the same occasion, the diplomat welcomed the efforts of the Personal Envoy of the UN Secretary-General for the Moroccan Sahara, Staffan de Mistura, aimed at facilitating the relaunch of the political process under the exclusive auspices of the United Nations.

He called on the main actors in this regional dispute for greater engagement in order to reach a realistic and lasting political solution, in accordance with international law and the relevant resolutions adopted by the UN Security Council and General Assembly.

RT/ac/Sf/APA

a6789.t:
La suppression de l'agence US d'aide au développement (USAID), évoqué par Elon Musk, serait une bonne nouvelle pour la sécurité du continent africain et de la lutte contre le terrorisme, a déclaré sur X Adamu Garba, ex-sénateur nigérian.
L'agence US d'aide au développement soutient des opérations de déstabilisations sur le continent, a déclaré Adamu Garba, ex-sénateur nigérian, dans une vidéo publiée sur X.
Sans son soutien, des groupes terroristes comme Boko Haram ou l'État islamique en Afrique de l'Ouest pourraient se trouver à court d'armes, de munitions et de moyens de reconnaissance, a-t-il ajouté.
"C’est une des très bonnes nouvelles pour l’Afrique, car l’USAID est une arme de guerre non conventionnelle pour les forces spéciales américaines, qui utilisent des méthodes de manipulation psychologique et soutiennent l’insurrection et la guerre irrégulière contre les Africains", a-t-il déclaré.
Les programmes éducatifs ou sanitaires de l'USAID ne sont qu'un masque, qui cache une volonté de "désorganiser" les pays africains, pour continuer de les exploiter et de servir un agenda américain, a-t-il indiqué.
Source: https://fr.sputniknews.africa/
a6789.en:
The end of USAID will bring peace to Africa, according to a Nigerian presidential candidate

The elimination of the US development aid agency (USAID), raised by Elon Musk, would be good news for the security of the African continent and for the fight against terrorism, Adamu Garba, a former Nigerian senator, declared on X.

The US development aid agency supports destabilisation operations on the continent, Adamu Garba, a former Nigerian senator, declared in a video published on X.

Without its support, terrorist groups such as Boko Haram or Islamic State in West Africa could find themselves short of weapons, ammunition and reconnaissance means, he added.

"This is one of the very good pieces of news for Africa, because USAID is an unconventional weapon of war for American special forces, which use methods of psychological manipulation and support insurgency and irregular warfare against Africans," he declared.

USAID's educational or health programmes are only a mask, which conceals a desire to "disorganise" African countries, in order to continue exploiting them and to serve an American agenda, he indicated.

Source: https://fr.sputniknews.africa/

a6802.t:
Aujourd'hui, dans le camp de réfugiés de Kakuma, j'ai rencontré Abdulaziz Lugazo, qui préside une coopérative d'agriculteurs produisant des cultures résistantes à la sécheresse telles que les épinards, le gombo et le chou vert. Abdulaziz a grandi dans la ferme familiale en Somalie et, lorsqu'il a été contraint de fuir en 1990, il n'a jamais pensé qu'il pourrait à nouveau cultiver la terre. Aujourd'hui, il peut travailler avec d'autres réfugiés et des agriculteurs kényans sur des terres fournies par le gouvernement, et il gagne suffisamment d'argent pour payer les livres et les uniformes scolaires de ses enfants.
Abdulaziz était impatient d'utiliser ses compétences pour aider ses compatriotes réfugiés et travailler au sein de la communauté kényane qui l'accueillait. Grâce aux politiques de plus en plus inclusives du Kénya à Kakuma, il a eu la possibilité de contribuer et de réussir.
Le Kenya et les Kényans accueillent généreusement des réfugiés depuis plus de 30 ans. Au cours de mes innombrables visites dans le pays, j'ai pu constater l'impact des nombreuses mesures positives et concrètes prises pour améliorer les conditions de vie des réfugiés et des communautés d'accueil.
Je profite de cette visite particulière pour souligner au reste du monde que nous pouvons - et devons - faire davantage pour offrir de l'espoir, des opportunités et des solutions aux réfugiés, où qu'ils se trouvent et quel que soit le contexte. Le Kenya montre que c'est possible.
L'intégration des réfugiés dans les communautés où ils ont trouvé la sécurité est le moyen le plus efficace de les aider à redémarrer leur vie et à contribuer à la croissance des pays qui les accueillent.
Concrètement, cela signifie qu'il faut veiller à ce que les réfugiés puissent postuler à des emplois, s'inscrire dans des écoles et accéder à des services tels que le logement et les soins de santé. Il s'agit également de favoriser un sentiment d'appartenance et d'accueil qui redonne de l'espoir aux réfugiés déracinés.
Le gouvernement kényan est prêt à mettre en œuvre des politiques innovantes et inclusives qui permettront à une grande partie du demi-million de réfugiés et de demandeurs d'asile de travailler et de vivre aux côtés des Kényans. Cela favorisera l'autonomie, la croissance économique et la réduction de la dépendance à l'égard de l'aide humanitaire.
Au Hcr, l'Agence des Nations unies pour les réfugiés, nous savons que l'intégration est le meilleur moyen de soutenir les réfugiés en exil, de les préparer afin qu'ils puissent contribuer à la reconstruction de leur pays lorsque les conditions leur permettront de rentrer, ou de s'épanouir s'ils sont réinstallés dans un autre pays.
Mais les pays d'accueil ne peuvent y parvenir seuls. Le reste de la communauté internationale doit intervenir et fournir les ressources financières nécessaires à la mise en œuvre de ces politiques progressistes. Nous avons constaté d'énormes progrès dans ce domaine au cours des dernières années, grâce à la générosité exceptionnelle des donateurs, à des approches novatrices en matière de financement et à des investissements considérables de la part de la Banque mondiale, des banques régionales de développement et d'autres institutions financières internationales. Mais il est clair qu'il faut faire plus.
Il est temps que nous nous engagions tous à inclure les réfugiés dans nos communautés à tous les niveaux - dans nos écoles, sur nos lieux de travail, dans nos systèmes de soins de santé et au-delà, comme le fait le gouvernement kényan, afin que les réfugiés puissent retrouver l'espoir loin de chez eux.
Nous devons également reconnaître les défis auxquels sont confrontés les pays d'accueil dans un monde en mal de paix. Le plus souvent, ce sont les communautés frontalières qui continuent à recevoir et à héberger les personnes fuyant la violence. Les pays voisins du Soudan sont un autre exemple de cette solidarité. De nombreux pays d'accueil comme eux ont la volonté d'accueillir et d'intégrer les réfugiés, mais ont besoin de beaucoup plus d'investissements et de soutien pour y parvenir.
Malheureusement, dans le monde divisé d'aujourd'hui, les solutions à long terme pour les personnes forcées de fuir restent pitoyablement rares, laissant un grand nombre des 35 millions de réfugiés dans le monde dans l'incertitude.
C'est pourquoi, en cette Journée mondiale des réfugiés, je conclus en appelant les dirigeants à se montrer à la hauteur de leur responsabilité de négocier la paix afin que la violence cesse et que les réfugiés puissent rentrer chez eux en toute sécurité et de leur plein gré.
Je demande aux gouvernements d'accroître les possibilités de réinstallation pour les réfugiés qui en ont désespérément besoin.
Et j'appelle les États à adopter des politiques qui exploitent l'énorme potentiel des réfugiés à contribuer à la vie sociale, économique et politique des pays qui les accueillent. Nous ne connaissons que trop bien le coût de l'inaction : un monde où les déplacements forcés sont les plus nombreux de l'histoire. Nous ne pouvons pas laisser cette situation perdurer.
a6802.en:
Today, in the Kakuma refugee camp, I met Abdulaziz Lugazo, who chairs a cooperative of farmers producing drought-resistant crops such as spinach, okra and collard greens. Abdulaziz grew up on the family farm in Somalia and, when he was forced to flee in 1990, he never thought he would be able to work the land again. Today, he can work with other refugees and with Kenyan farmers on land provided by the government, and he earns enough money to pay for his children's school books and uniforms.

Abdulaziz was eager to use his skills to help his fellow refugees and to work within the Kenyan community that had welcomed him. Thanks to Kenya's increasingly inclusive policies in Kakuma, he has had the opportunity to contribute and to succeed.

Kenya and Kenyans have been generously hosting refugees for more than 30 years. In the course of my countless visits to the country, I have been able to see the impact of the many positive and concrete measures taken to improve the living conditions of refugees and host communities.

I take advantage of this particular visit to stress to the rest of the world that we can — and must — do more to offer hope, opportunities and solutions to refugees, wherever they are and whatever the context. Kenya shows that it is possible.

Integrating refugees into the communities where they have found safety is the most effective way to help them restart their lives and to contribute to the growth of the countries that host them.

Concretely, this means ensuring that refugees can apply for jobs, enrol in schools and access services such as housing and health care. It also means fostering a sense of belonging and welcome that restores hope to uprooted refugees.

The Kenyan government is ready to implement innovative and inclusive policies that will allow a large share of the half a million refugees and asylum seekers to work and live alongside Kenyans. This will promote self-reliance, economic growth and reduced dependence on humanitarian aid.

At UNHCR, the United Nations Refugee Agency, we know that inclusion is the best way to support refugees in exile, to prepare them so that they can contribute to rebuilding their country when conditions allow them to return, or to thrive if they are resettled in another country.

But host countries cannot achieve this alone. The rest of the international community must step in and provide the financial resources needed to implement these progressive policies. We have seen enormous progress in this area in recent years, thanks to exceptional donor generosity, innovative approaches to financing and considerable investments from the World Bank, the regional development banks and other international financial institutions. But it is clear that more must be done.

It is time for all of us to commit to including refugees in our communities at every level — in our schools, in our workplaces, in our health care systems and beyond, as the Kenyan government is doing — so that refugees can recover hope far from home.

We must also recognize the challenges faced by host countries in a world short of peace. More often than not, it is border communities that continue to receive and shelter people fleeing violence. Sudan's neighbouring countries are another example of this solidarity. Many host countries like them have the will to welcome and integrate refugees, but need far more investment and support in order to do so.

Unfortunately, in today's divided world, long-term solutions for people forced to flee remain pitifully rare, leaving a great many of the world's 35 million refugees in uncertainty.

That is why, on this World Refugee Day, I conclude by calling on leaders to live up to their responsibility to negotiate peace so that the violence stops and refugees can return home safely and voluntarily.

I ask governments to increase resettlement opportunities for refugees who desperately need them.

And I call on States to adopt policies that harness the enormous potential of refugees to contribute to the social, economic and political life of the countries that host them. We know all too well the cost of inaction: a world with the highest levels of forced displacement in history. We cannot let this situation continue.

A total of 180,000 people living with HIV are now accessing life-saving antiretroviral treatment across 264 health facilities in Benue State.
The Commissioner for Health and Human Services, Dr Yanmar Ortese, made the disclosure while commending the APIN public health initiative and the United States Centre for Disease Control (US CDC) for donating a cutting-edge Molecular Laboratory and a Polymerase Chain Reaction machine to the Federal Medical Centre (FMC) in Makurdi, the state capital.
Ortese was full of praises for the US President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) for its support to the state in the fight against HIV/AIDS.
“Your investment in our healthcare system has been instrumental in transforming HIV from a death sentence to a manageable chronic disease.

“Through PEPFAR’s support, over 180,000 people living with HIV are now accessing life-saving antiretroviral treatment across 264 health facilities in our state.
“The prevention of mother-to-child transmission programme has also ensured the birth of approximately 8,000 HIV-negative babies annually,” Ortese stated.
Earlier, the FMC Medical Director, Kortor, said the donation of the machine was a development which marked a significant step forward in the commitment to enhancing healthcare services and bolstering the capacity to combat infectious diseases in the state.
The Acting Country Director, US CDC-Nigeria, Suzanne Theroux, at the commissioning of the project, presented a laboratory accreditation certificate number ISO15189:2012 to the medical director of FMC, Professor Joseph Kortor.
Theroux expressed confidence that the donation would improve healthcare for HIV patients and others suffering from chronic diseases.

a7445.t:
In Nankhumwa Village in Chiradzulu District, visible changes are beginning to take hold. New iron-sheet roofs glint in the sun where thatch once sagged.
The sound of construction tools echoes across the village and conversations now centre on farming plans and business ideas rather than food shortages or petty theft.
For many residents, this shift marks the beginning of a new chapter.
The transformation began with the arrival of unconditional cash transfers. These were not loans or handouts tied to restrictive conditions but a demonstration of trust in people’s ability to make the best choices for their families.
Forty-five-year-old Befia Jalison explains how difficult it once was to put food on the table.
- Advertisement -
“For the first time, three-quarters of the people here can afford to eat three meals a day,” Jalison says.
Chiradzulu is one of the districts in Malawi experiencing significant hunger due to a combination of factors including drought, erratic rainfall and limited access to agricultural inputs.
“Crime has gone down. Even our houses look different. You see iron sheets everywhere now. Things are good now. Really good,” she adds.
Sixty-year-old Bertha Billiat knows this change all too well. A tomato and maize farmer, she used to struggle to make ends meet, often earning as little as K800 from her produce.
- Advertisement -
- Advertisement -
“Now, I make K80,000. My husband and I decided to buy fertiliser and start keeping livestock. In two years, we will have five cattle and some pigs,” Billiat says.
She has also introduced crop rotation to her fields and has harvested five bags from winter cropping for the first time.
Billiat no longer worries about thieves stealing her harvest and she feels empowered by receiving money directly into her account.
For Lucy Joseph, the changes have meant dignity and new possibilities. Working as a housemaid in Manja, Blantyre, she has stopped sending money home to support her mother and two children.
“Before, life was so difficult. Now my mother can buy food and she has started a small business,” she says.
Village Head Mwamadi says the entire community has been transformed.
“I reroofed my house, which was leaking during the rainy season. I managed to buy a motorbike and I even managed to buy land,” he says, standing near a newly built nursery school.
The local leader adds that it is now easy to tell parents to send their children to school because they can afford it.
Once a potato farmer, the chief states that hunger and crime have both sharply declined. Disputes are also easier to resolve.
He notes that domestic violence often occurs when men lack income and he expresses hope that new economic opportunities would reduce tension in households.
Mwamadi now uses his motorbike and a newly acquired fridge for small business ventures.
In one corner of the village, Ketelena Witness points to her neighbour’s home. “John Kholowo now has green iron sheets on his roof,” she says. “We are helping each other buy roofing sheets.”
Nearby, 60-year-old Gogo Mwayi recently slept on a bed for the first time in her life.
Over the past 15 years, Malawi has received an estimated $16.5 billion in development assistance. Yet poverty remains persistently high, with 70 percent of Malawians still living below the extreme poverty line of $2.15 per day.
Climate change, declining agricultural productivity and frequent economic shocks keep many families trapped in cycles of hunger and debt.
In 2019, however, the nonprofit organisation GiveDirectly began working in partnership with the Government of Malawi to change the approach to aid.
Instead of distributing goods or services, they send cash directly to recipients with no conditions attached.
Since then, the organisation has delivered more than $101 million to over 226,000 households in some of the country’s poorest areas.
“Our aim is to lift every person in Malawi above the extreme poverty line. We believe people know best what they need. We simply give them the resources and the dignity to decide for themselves.” External Relations Senior Manager at GiveDirectly, Martin Kalima, says.
Across 11 districts and four cities, families are using the money to start businesses, pay school fees, buy livestock and improve their homes.
In places such as Nankhumwa, the results are visible and deeply personal. This is proof that a small amount of cash, placed in the right hands, can ignite a chain reaction of hope and resilience
